newsitem.title: USA: Ore. hearing on Enron, PGE set for Friday.
newsitem.headline: Ore. hearing on Enron, PGE set for Friday.

text.p: Oregon Public Utilities Commission (OPUC) will hold a hearing Friday morning aimed at clearing the way for a compromise on terms for the merger of Enron Corp and Portland General Electric Co.
Tom Riordan, senior analyst at the OPUC, said the hearing will be "an opportunity for all parties to come before the OPUC so it can give us some direction."
The OPUC staff has approved the merger with several conditions, including a $47.4 million annual rate reduction for Portland General customers for the first four years after the merger.
Enron and Portland General, however, say cost savings from their combination will amount to around $3 million a year.
A settlement conference in late January ended with no progress on a compromise and led to the special hearing being scheduled for Friday.
"Nothing has been proposed that is different from what the positions were a few weeks ago," Riordan said on Thursday.
"We will certainly entertain any additional information, but I am not aware of any communication so far," he added.
Officials at Enron and PGE could not be reached for comment on Thursday.
The hearing is set to begin Friday at 0900 PST/1200 EST/1700 GMT in Salem, Ore. The OPUC expects to make a final decision on the merger on or about March 17.
